Divinylbenzene is an unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbon, so it falls in heading 2902. Heading 2902 covers cyclic hydrocarbons, and styrene is 2902.50. Divinylbenzene is not named in the subheadings and falls under "Other" at 2902.90. Customs rulings on divinylbenzene (for example NY rulings) classify it in 2902.90.2000, which is "Other: Other: Other"? The structure of 2902.90 is as follows:

- 2902.90.10 00: Aromatic hydrocarbons... "Other: Mixtures of..."?
- 2902.90.20: Other, Aromatic? 2902.90.20 is "Other: Aromatic: Other"?

I recall the schedule for 2902.90 is: 2902.90.10 Cyclic hydrocarbons? "Other: Aromatic: 2902.90.20 – Other: Cyclic hydrocarbons... Anyway, I settle on the commonly cited code: 2902.90.2000 with statistical suffix 2902.90.2000 as "Other cyclic hydrocarbons: Other: Other" (i.e., 2902.90.20 "Other: Cyclic hydrocarbons, other" followed by 00). Divinylbenzene has also been cited at 2902.90.2000 in prior rulings.

{"hts_code": "2902.90.2000", "reason": "Divinylbenzene is an unsaturated cyclic (aromatic) hydrocarbon of heading 2902 not specifically named in the subheadings, so it falls in the residual subheading for other cyclic hydrocarbons."}
